focus: Explain binary-response logistic probability from a linear score z = intercept + weight times input and p = 1/(1+exp(-z)). Let learners change the score components and compare z, odds exp(z), and the resulting probability, emphasizing that the probability remains between zero and one.
audience: A second-year engineering undergraduate familiar with linear functions, exponentials, and probability.
excerpt: Paraphrase, not a quotation: the paper defines sigmoid sigma(z)=1/(1+exp(-z)) and a logistic binary-probability model. This case uses the one-feature linear-score specialization and displays odds as a derived intermediate, not as a claim quoted from the paper.
section: Are Logistic Models Really Interpretable? (2024), PDF p. 2, Notation and Definition 2.1: sigmoid sigma(z)=1/(1+exp(-z)) and logistic additive model. The linked primary PDF is openly readable.
